note: For a convex quadrilateral ABCD, let O be the unique intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of diagonals AC and BD. If ABCE is a partner and E is the reflection of D across the perpendicular bisector l of AC, then O lies on l and is fixed by the reflection, so OE=OD. Since O also lies on the perpendicular bisector of BD, OD=OB, hence OE=OB; therefore O lies on the perpendicular bisector of BE. Together with O on the perpendicular bisector of AC and uniqueness for the convex quadrilateral ABCE, this proves the same O persists. This avoids the misleading shortcut that segment BD itself reflects to BE when B need not lie on l.

Each move preserves the multiset of radii from O because three vertices remain and the replaced vertex has equal O-distance. It preserves the unordered multiset of side lengths: AB and BC remain; reflection swaps A with C and D with E, giving CD=AE and DA=CE.

Finiteness reconstruction: every cyclicly labeled quadrilateral in the sequence has four vertex radii drawn from a fixed finite multiset R and four consecutive side lengths drawn from a fixed finite multiset S. Normalize O at the origin and the first vertex on the positive x-axis. Given the previous vertex, the next radius, and the intervening side length, the next vertex is an intersection of two circles, hence at most two choices. Thus each choice of four radii and four side lengths yields finitely many configurations up to rotation; since there are finitely many such choices, only finitely many congruence classes occur.
